hints.title: Reverse Splitting Process
hints.text: Consider the last split into two pieces of length one. That split required an adjacent pair of elements.

hints.title: Core Invariant
hints.text: For any array of length greater than two, a valid splitting sequence exists if and only if there exists some adjacent pair whose sum is at least m.

hints.title: Base Cases
hints.text: If the array has length one or two, it can trivially be split into single-element subarrays without restriction.

hints.title: Implementation

complexity.notes: Single pass adjacent pair sum check.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Top-down memoized interval DP takes O(n^3) when a constant-space adjacent pair invariant exists.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(1) space with no auxiliary allocations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Identify the critical adjacent-pair condition that guarantees recursive splittability.
